subject: Custodian storage warranty and operational delete evidence — clarifications
messages:
From: Eve Chen <eve.chen@lumahq.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Luma Legal <contracts@lumahq.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on customer-controlled store & deletion evidence for Private VPC

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams raised a couple of follow-up questions focused on how Redwood will demonstrate deletion and residency guarantees for a private (VPC) deployment where we manage the storage. Specific asks:

1) If Luma requests a tenant wipe, what artifact(s) do you provide as proof the data was destroyed — for both live storage and backups/snapshots?
2) Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for the tenant store and how does KMS rotation interact with your proof-of-delete process?
3) Can Redwood produce a notarized or signed attestation of deletion for compliance audits (HIPAA/ SOC2)?
4) How do you prevent replication to other regions during a delete/sunset flow?

Appreciate a short, concrete answer we can share with our legal and infosec folks.

Best,
Eve
Director, Cloud Security
Luma Health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Eve Chen <eve.chen@lumahq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on customer-controlled store & deletion evidence for Private VPC

Hi Eve —

Thanks — this is a great set of questions. High level answers below, followed by a suggested evidence checklist we can produce. I copied Marissa (Customer Success) and Karthik (Private deployments lead) for any operational notes.

1) Proof of tenant wipe:
- For live storage we provide a deletion manifest (CSV) with object keys/paths, deletion timestamps, operator id, and cryptographic hash of the last tombstoned object metadata.
- For snapshots/backups we include a snapshot manifest showing snapshot ids, retention window, and a verified wipe timestamp once snapshot tombstones complete.
- If required, we can include a chain-of-custody export that shows which storage servers processed the wipe (IP, instance id) within the VPC.

2) Customer-managed keys (BYOK):
- Yes. We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) using customer-managed CMKs. When a customer rotates a key, Redwood records the key version used for each encryption envelope and includes those identifiers in the deletion manifest.
- Important: If the customer revokes key access (e.g., scheduled deletion of a CMK), that is considered an additional control for 'crypto-erase' — we will document the rotation/revoke events in the audit export.

3) Attestation & notarization:
- We can provide a signed attestation (PDF) that summarizes the wipe, includes manifests, and is signed by an authorized Redwood operations lead.
- For higher assurance (legal requirement), we support a third-party notarization workflow — we can coordinate a notary (or joint witness with Luma) and include that statement as part of the delivery.

4) Preventing cross-region replication: 
- For Private/VPC deployments, the default is single-region replication within the customer-controlled storage. Replication to other regions requires explicit customer configuration or a separate replication job.
- During a sunset/wipe request we disable replication drivers at the control plane level and confirm via runbook that no DR/replication tasks are in flight — that confirmation is part of the snapshot manifest.

Evidence checklist (we can produce these artifacts within 3–5 business days once the wipe request is accepted):
- deletion_manifest_YYYYMMDD.csv (object path, hash, ts, operator)
- snapshot_manifest_YYYYMMDD.json (snapshot ids, retention metadata, tombstone ts)
- kms_rotation_audit.csv (key id, version, rotation_ts referenced)
- signed_attestation.pdf (signed by Redwood ops)
- chain_of_custody_log.csv (optional, infra-level evidence)

I attached our standard VPC wipe playbook and an example KMS rotation report to this email for reference. Let us know if your auditors need notarization or a witnessed deletion.

—Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc_wipe_playbook.pdf (application/pdf), kms_rotation_audit.csv (text/csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on customer-controlled store & deletion evidence for Private VPC

Adding a few operational clarifications from CS/ops perspective:

- We require a signed request from a named customer admin (email proof) before initiating any tenant wipe — this becomes part of the chain-of-custody.
- For backup retention windows: if a backup snapshot is in a multi-day retention hold (customer policy), we will only mark it for deletion after the retention expiry unless the customer confirms immediate purge. If immediate purge is required for compliance, we escalate to a manual process with notarized confirmation.
- For customers using BYOK, recommend scheduling a key revocation only after we confirm manifest generation. Revoking keys early will make retrieval impossible and may be considered the strongest form of erase, but you should confirm with your legal team first.

Small ask for Eve: can you confirm whether Luma's policy requires an independent notary or if a Redwood-signed attestation is acceptable? That will affect timing/cost.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
